title: Foreign Currency Lending, Balance Sheet Mismatch and Legislative Settlements

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: Between 2004 and 2008, hundreds of thousands of Hungarian households took out Swiss franc loans, attracted by lower interest rates than on forint loans. When the forint weakened sharply against the franc during the global crisis, the monthly instalments of many borrowers rose steeply, and the foreign-currency loans became a widely discussed social and legal problem.

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: The Curia ruled in 2014 (a uniformity decision, *jogegységi határozat*) that certain terms in these contracts, among them exchange rate spreads and unilateral rate increases, were unfair contract terms (*tisztességtelen szerződési feltétel*). Laws passed in 2014 then settled the accounts and provided for the conversion of the loans to forints (*forintosítás*), carried out in early 2015.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A svájci frank erősödése sok háztartásnál megnövelte a törlesztőrészleteket.
The strengthening of the Swiss franc raised the instalments of many households.
A Kúria jogegységi határozata tisztességtelennek nyilvánította az árfolyamrést.
The Curia's uniformity decision declared the exchange rate spread unfair.
A devizahitelek forintosítása csökkentette a rendszerszintű pénzügyi kockázatot.
The conversion of FX loans into forints reduced systemic financial risk.
